subject: Production: HelioHealth inference degradation — prefetch/KV congestion
messages:
From: Megan Lin <megan.lin@heliohealth.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@heliohealth.com
Date: 2027-09-18T07:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike: 6-10s p95 latency and 5% generation errors since 07:00 PT

Hi Redwood support,

Since around 07:00 PT we've seen a sharp degradation on our production routes (model: gpt-small-opt-prod). P95 latency jumped from ~400ms to 6-10s and generation errors have gone to ~5% (timeouts and "KV fetch failed"). Throughput for our ingestion pipeline is dropping as retries pile up.

This is customer-impacting — whole search assistant flow times out and some pages are erroring. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (deploys, config pushes)? We're in a scheduled rollout window this week but hadn't pushed anything at 06:00.

Attached are a snippet of our request IDs and the first 2 error traces. Please treat as P1.

Thanks,
Megan
Megan Lin
Engineering Manager, HelioHealth
[attachment: helio_err_samples.txt]
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: megan.lin@heliohealth.com
Cc: vivek.kulkarni, grace.oconnor, ben.carter
Date: 2027-09-18T07:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 6-10s p95 latency and 5% generation errors since 07:00 PT

Hi Megan — thanks for the fast report and the samples. We're treating this as P1 and have the on-call infra team investigating.

Quick context: there were no planned deploys at 06:00 PT in the hosted control plane, but we did observe an unusual prefetch/pinned-key access spike starting 06:55 PT that correlates with your request IDs. Early hypothesis is KV cache churn causing head-of-line (HOL) blocking in the prefetch lane for your tenant's routes.

What we'll do now:
- Run a KV trace across the affected hosts and collect prefetch metrics (kv_trace_20270918.tar.gz) — attaching when complete.
- Temporarily widen the hot-lane queue for your tenant to reduce HOL blocking.
- If immediate relief isn't seen in 10–15m we'll failover a subset of traffic to a compatible model variant with a warm prefix cache.

Can you confirm any traffic pattern changes on your side (bulk backfills, batch scoring) around 06:45–07:05 PT?

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Megan Lin <megan.lin@heliohealth.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@heliohealth.com
Date: 2027-09-18T07:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 6-10s p95 latency and 5% generation errors since 07:00 PT

Hannah —
We started a periodic batch enrichment at 06:50 PT (small window, ~30 requests/s for 5 minutes) to refresh patient context caches. It was intended to be low-impact but may have aligned badly with daytime traffic.

If widening the hot-lane helps we'll stand down the enrichment job immediately. Please keep us posted.

Megan
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni, grace.oconnor, hannah.schmitt, laura.bennett
Date: 2027-09-18T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: HelioHealth P1 — initial KV trace and mitigation

Team — quick summary of what the traces show (attached to this mail): kv_trace_20270918.tar.gz contains three host traces and a prefetch histogram. Highlights: 
- Massive burst of prefix pin requests for HelioHealth tenant between 06:50–06:56 PT.
- Prefetch thread pool on two hosts saturated; KV misses spiked leading to synchronous backend fetches.
- Observed HOL blocking where a hot prefix fetch held prefetch worker threads, stalling subsequent prefix lookups (queue depth increased x12).
- Small fraction (~0.6%) of requests experienced KV timeout -> model stack retried, producing the 5% visible error rate due to amplification under backpressure.

Immediate mitigations applied at 07:10 PT: widened hot-lane concurrency for HelioHealth and enabled aggressive KV read-timeout fallback (300ms). Early telemetry shows p95 dropping from ~8s to ~1.2s; error rate moving toward baseline (still ~1% as retries drain).

Next recommended actions for durable fix:
1) Add a tenant-scoped prefetch rate limiter to prevent burst-induced exhaust of prefetch pool.
2) Introduce a soft queue cap to avoid HOL blocking by allowing low-priority requests to take degraded path rather than waiting.
3) For HelioHealth specifically: recommend they stagger batch refreshes to avoid overlap with daytime peaks (we can propose a throttled schedule).

I created JIRA SUP-4521 to track the permanent changes and the customer RCA. I'm proposing a 48-hour action plan and an exec sync if the customer requests credits or SLA exceptions.

Attachments: kv_trace_20270918.tar.gz

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SW Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett, grace.oconnor, ben.carter, hannah.schmitt
Cc: sales@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-18T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Exec note — HelioHealth P1 escalation and ask for customer-facing plan

Laura/Grace —
HelioHealth just filed a P1 due to a KV-prefetch-induced HOL blocking event after a customer-side batch refresh aligned with peak traffic. Hannah/Ben applied immediate mitigations (hot-lane widen, fallback timeouts) and we have partial recovery.

Customer impact: elevated p95 and ~5% visible errors at peak, now reduced to ~1% after mitigations. HelioHealth is asking for:
- A clear short-term playbook (what we did, what we'll do next 48h)
- A proposal for a schedule to avoid batch collisions (we offered a throttled refresh window)
- Fast decision on whether to offer a one-off credit for the incident window (they are enterprise; we should consider relationship optics)

Proposed customer-facing plan (I drafted an MAPP — mutual action plan — and attached):
- 0–2h: Mitigations applied and monitoring. (done)
- 2–24h: Implement tenant-scoped prefetch limiter + emergency warm prefix seeding for HelioHealth routes.
- 24–48h: Deploy a soft-queue cap + update prefetch worker autosize heuristic.
- RCA & follow-up: publish RCA and post-mortem, propose credit if SLA breach confirmed.

Asking for quick guidance: 1) Approve the 24–48h engineering changes as a priority for infra, 2) Let's offer a goodwill credit of one week of hosted tokens if we confirm error window impact — is that acceptable?

I'll coordinate an exec sync if needed. I want to keep this tight and to the point for the customer.

Vivek
VP, Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference
[attachment: helio_mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf]
From: Megan Lin <megan.lin@heliohealth.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@heliohealth.com
Date: 2027-09-19T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: HelioHealth inference degradation — prefetch/KV congestion

Vivek/Hannah —
Thanks for the rapid response and the clear plan. The widening of the lane gave immediate relief and our UX teams report much fewer errors. We accept the proposed throttled refresh schedule and would appreciate the one-week token credit while you complete your RCA.

We'll pause the nightly full-context refresh while you roll the tenant limiter and soft-queue cap. Please share the post-mortem when ready; we prefer a short exec summary plus technical appendix.

Appreciate the quick ownership.

— Megan
Megan Lin
Engineering Manager, HelioHealth
